text:
Tage Thompson scored three times, including two goals 15 seconds apart late in the second period, and the Sabres turned a 3-0 hole's worth of trouble into a 7-6 win over the Ducks at Honda Center. BUF trailed 3-1 in the first before storming back, the kind of two-goal comeback that usually needs a quiet night from the other side. It didn't get one. Thompson, drafted 26th overall by St. Louis in 2016 out of the University of Connecticut, also added two assists. Peyton Krebs picked up three assists of his own.

The score undersells how the game was played. Our numbers give ANA a 65% chance to have won, the share of simulated replays of every shot that the Ducks take. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, favored ANA 3.96 to 3.34, and the Ducks led the first period 1.90 to 0.48 on that measure. Noah Ostlund's goal for BUF came on a 2% chance. Both goalies struggled: Ville Husso allowed 7 on 31 shots, about four more than the chances against him deserved, while Colten Ellis gave up 6 on 35. Cutter Gauthier, the fifth overall pick in 2022, scored twice on 10 shots.

ANA got a first NHL goal from Roger McQueen, the 10th pick in 2025, and pushed late, scoring twice in the final 68 seconds to make it 7-6. The facts give us no records or streaks for either team, so all we can say is that the Sabres held on and the Ducks left with a loss they came close to erasing. We'd watch whether Husso's night is an outlier or a pattern.
